turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I’ve been having trouble explaining things clearly. Like at work, when I’m trying to go over inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words kind of jump around—from trucks to Thursdays to the church grill, then something about my boss’s tone—and people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. It’s been bothering me.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient describes speech that jumps between unrelated topics and is difficult for others to follow.

turns.doctor_question: Did this trouble with your speech start suddenly, over a day or two, or has it been building up gradually over weeks or months?
turns.patient_response: It’s been gradual. I’d say it’s been building over maybe 11 months or so, since the new district manager came in and started pushing harder on forecasts and schedules. It didn’t just happen overnight.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices that others don't hear, or having strong beliefs that others seem to think are untrue or overly suspicious?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed voices or anything like that. As for beliefs… I don’t know, I’ve been feeling like people don’t understand me, but I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient states they have not really noticed voices or anything like that, denying hallucination-like experiences.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past several months, have you had any stretches of time where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or low for days at a time, separate from just feeling frustrated at work?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated and worn down when things at work don’t come out right, but I can’t say I’ve had days where my mood was unusually high or really low in a separate way. Not that I’ve noticed.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient denies having days of unusually low mood separate from work-related frustration.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient denies having days of unusually high or irritable mood separate from work-related frustration.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any other physical symptoms along with this speech trouble, like headaches, weakness or numbness on one side, vision changes, or difficulty understanding what other people say to you?
turns.patient_response: I haven’t really noticed anything like that. No… I don’t think I’ve had headaches or one-sided weakness or vision problems. And I understand people okay, mostly. It’s more that getting my own words out gets difficult sometimes.

turns.doctor_question: When this happens, is the main problem that you can't find or recall the specific word you want to say, or is it more that your thoughts jump to unrelated topics even though the words themselves come out fine?
turns.patient_response: It’s more that my thoughts jump around. I usually know the words, but when I’m trying to explain something like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, I’ll start talking about the trucks, then Thursday, then something about the church grill, then my boss’s tone. It makes sense in my head for a second, but people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient reports thoughts jumping among unrelated topics and speech that others cannot follow, consistent with disorganized thinking/speech.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any history of head injury, seizures, or neurological illness, or do you use alcohol or any recreational drugs regularly?
turns.patient_response: Not that I know of. I haven’t had a head injury or seizures, at least nothing I’d call that. No neurological illness that I’m aware of. I don’t use drugs, and I don’t really drink regularly.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any changes in your interest in socializing with friends or family, or in how much emotion you show, since this all started?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to that. I still talk to family when I need to, but I guess I don’t know if I’m acting different emotionally. No one’s really sat me down and said that, at least.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory, like forgetting recent conversations or getting confused about the day or where you are?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed getting lost about what day it is or where I am. I might forget little things like anyone does, but not recent conversations in a way that stands out to me.

turns.doctor_question: Since this started, have you noticed your job performance or ability to handle daily responsibilities getting worse, like missing deadlines, being written up, or struggling to complete tasks you used to manage fine?
turns.patient_response:
Yes. Work has definitely gotten harder. I used to run the busy weekend shifts, but they don’t really trust me with those anymore. After my last performance review, my boss told me if things don’t improve I could be suspended.

And at home, my wife has had to pick up things I used to take care of, because people were getting uncomfortable or confused around me. It’s been... embarrassing, honestly.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned feeling like people don't understand you—do you ever feel that people are specifically watching you, talking about you behind your back, or trying to harm you in some way, even when there's no clear proof of that?
turns.patient_response: I don’t really know. I mean, I feel like people don’t understand me, but I can’t say I’ve got proof they’re watching me or trying to hurt me. Sometimes I wonder what people are thinking, but I don’t know that it’s anything like that.

turns.doctor_question: Have you or others noticed you doing things that seem unusual or out of place, like unusual body movements, odd clothing choices, or behavior that doesn't fit the situation?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess so. At work, sometimes I’ll catch myself pacing the same aisle, or straightening the same row of batteries over and over. Other times I’m just standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand while the associates are waiting for me to tell them what to do. It feels… out of place, and I don’t always realize it right away.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes repetitive pacing and straightening the same items, as well as standing unresponsively with a clipboard while associates await direction, and recognizes these behaviors as out of place.
